conventions.convention: N≥3, V=C² with ordered basis e_up,e_down, and chain factors are in left-to-right site order. R_aj(u)=uI+iP_aj; T_a(u)=R_aN(u)⋯R_a1(u), with the rightmost factor acting first. The transfer matrix is the ordinary auxiliary partial trace.
U sends v₁⊗⋯⊗v_N to v_N⊗v₁⊗⋯⊗v_(N−1), moving a site state one position to the right.
Periodic bonds use P_(N,N+1)=P_(N,1); in the omitted-factor calculation P_(0,1)=P_(N,1). The spectral parameter and its derivative are dimensionless.

The shifted operators are L_aj(u)=R_aj(u−i/2), with auxiliary entries A,B,C,D and reference vector Ω=e_up raised to the Nth tensor power. Regular data have 0≤M≤N, finite distinct roots avoiding ±i/2, no pairwise difference ±i, the displayed Bethe equations, and a nonzero B-product vector. For M=0 all products are empty and Ψ=Ω.
The exchange Hamiltonian is H_N=J∑P_(j,j+1)+cI for real J,c. Its Pauli normalization is P=(I+X⊗X+Y⊗Y+Z⊗Z)/2. J and c have joule units only when interpreted as physical energies.
One-magnon Fourier vectors use positive phases exp(ik_m j), k_m=2πm/N, 0≤m<N, and the example sets c=0.

load_bearing.statement: For N≥3, V=C² and u∈C, define R_aj(u)=uI+iP_aj, T_a(u)=R_aN(u)⋯R_a1(u), and t(u)=tr_a T_a(u), with rightmost-first composition and U(v₁⊗⋯⊗v_N)=v_N⊗v₁⊗⋯⊗v_(N−1).
With P_(N,N+1)=P_(N,1), t(0)=i^N U and i t′(0)t(0)⁻¹=∑_(j=1)^N P_(j,j+1). In particular, t(0) is invertible.
For every u,v∈C, [t(u),t(v)]=0. Near zero, M(u)=t(0)⁻¹t(u) has the analytic matrix logarithm with log M(0)=0; its Taylor-coefficient matrices commute pairwise and with every t(v).
With periodic bonds, i t′(0)t(0)⁻¹=∑P_(j,j+1). For real J,c, H_N=J∑P_(j,j+1)+cI is Hermitian and commutes with every t(u). The two-site swap equals (I+X⊗X+Y⊗Y+Z⊗Z)/2.

A regular on-shell Bethe datum is a tuple satisfying the stated root exclusions, Bethe equations, and nonzero-vector condition for Ψ=B(λ₁)⋯B(λ_M)Ω; no completeness or singular-root construction is asserted.

published_dependencies.used_for: Complex scalar and tensor-product conventions underlying the imported rational R-matrix definition.
Elementary tensor bases used to define flips and verify the finite operator identities on basis tensors.
The exact rational convention R(u)=uI+iP, tensor-leg flips, and rightmost-first composition.
The un-checked spectral Yang–Baxter identity with differences x−y, x−z, y−z; substituting x=u,y=v,z=0 supplies the local RTT relation. Its checked-identity diagram also agrees with its statement.

alerts.finding: The Definition says that g^L_(M,N) 'counts subspaces N′⊆L with N′≅N and L/N′≅M, or equivalently short exact sequences 0→N→L→M→0.' Counting actual sequences with fixed endpoint objects also counts choices of endpoint identifications. For M=N=F₃ and L=F₃², there are four eligible subspaces but sixteen such sequences. The subspace definition is unambiguous; the alternative wording needs an equivalence relation or a qualification that endpoint identifications are forgotten.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its items against the transfer suppliers. thm-qsmx-exchange-lie-weight-blocks F2 preserves R=uI+iP, monodromy order, auxiliary trace, and N≥3; F3 preserves the periodic exchange normalization and real-coupling hypotheses. Spin invariance is proved separately. The transfer page makes no converse Hall or categorical claim. The diagrams agree with the stated operator conventions.

Checked all four transport-page items. This is a declared page prerequisite without an item-level citation of a transfer theorem. The transport results use explicit local conservation, stationarity, conserved-overlap, and correlation-integrability hypotheses; they do not infer a thermodynamic Drude weight or diffusion from transfer commutativity. The transfer page likewise asserts no transport conclusion. The current-orientation and projection diagrams agree with their text.
